Newcastle's Coal Nightmare

By: Anina Peens | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
When real thirst kicks, will it be too late?

Unique Selling Point:
When they have come to take all our resources and return back to their countries, what will be left of our farms?

Summary:
It is about the future of our water and food security. If we keep forcing farmers off their land, who is going to provide food? If the mines damage one of our largest aquifers in the country, where are we going to get water?

OPENING: We see the valleys of wakkerstroom and we hear a man speaking, in Zulu…: we use to drink from these fountains when we were children. Now, they are drying up. We send our cattle here, but the fountains are slowly drying up.

We begin also, with his story…. How he wanted to be a commercial farmer and finally made it, saved his money and now the mines come….

Then we move to Newcastle, to the agricultural school… the farms and the game around newcaslte, vulentaba, the local government’s plan to expand tourism. But the mines.

Then paint a picture of the mines and what happens to coal. Expert opinion on the future of coal. How long a coal mine will be in an area? What they leave behind

Build the emotion around it and how it affects the earth and the people. How 50% of the country’s water comes from this area.

Then the problems with the mines, the frustrations they cause, the EIA’s that are just signed off in favor of the mines.

The small mines popping up and operating without proper paperwork.
Possible interaction with one such a mine.


Then back to the fight and what the communities are doing to protect what they have.

The zama zamas coming in the town, the towns never had a problem with that.

What is government doing?

Why are there 2500 applications? can anyone just apply? What is is mineral resources saying?

Why are we even talking about coal?

Press Release:


Digging for Coal
In KwaZulu-Natal, commercial farmers are on edge. While they own the land they farm on, government owns the minerals that lie underneath, and it’s giving scores of upstart coal companies prospecting licences and rights to mine. Tensions between farmers and mining groups in Newcastle are at an all-time high as the coal prospectors move in by the dozen to mine what’s left of the area’s coal reserve. For farmers, what’s equally concerning is the risk to vital water sources like the town’s main dam, which provides drinking water to hundreds of thousands of people. Who are these opportunistic mining companies and why are they being allowed to mine in sensitive and protected areas?
Producer: Anina Peens | Presenter: Erin Bates | Research: Laura Byrne

Script:


NEWCASTLE

PART 1

SOURCE: MVII_2883 and MVI_2888
UPSOUND; SOME KIND OF MEDITATIONAL MUSIC AND THE SHOT OF THE DRAKENSBERG TO CREATE A FEELING OF MAGNITUDE AND BEAUTY AND THEN THE FRESH WATER

SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312

“…right at the top where everything starts”

We’re with Angus Burns - an environmentalist with the World Wildlife Fund - in the Northern Drakensberg, where he works to get sites like these declared protected.

SUPER@ANGUS BURNG: WWF
SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312
MVI_2892
17:52:25:46
10 percent of the surface area of south Africa provides 50% of our water needs. That is our lifeblood

Securing the country’s drinking water is at the heart of Burns’ mission. (PAUSE) A daunting task around Newcastle in KZN.

VISUAL: COAL MINE

VO
Coal…
The backbone of the economy… but the dirtiest of any mining processes.

Many inexperienced yet ambitious mining companies want to cash in.
Creating a sight best appreciated from the air.

BREATHER? OR MOMENT

SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312
MVI_2892
17:50:42:21
“I’ve seen maps of Mpumalanga province and northern KZN. It’s just a puzzle of little dots and spots showing cadasters of farms that are under prospecting and mining rights and literally zero strategic thinking given to the location of these sites in relation to water source areas”

VO
In recent years, small operators have been popping up across a vast area stretching from Newcastle, across the border into Mpumalanga. Many of the permit holders are small businesses without much mining experience.

LINK/PROMO
SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312
MVI_2968
18:56:08:40
“We’re at the foothills of the Drakensberg and coal prospectors are carving into the earth down below. Question is, once they leave, is this just going to be a graveyard of coal mines?”

VO
Environmental impact assessments carried out before mining can start often don’t fully reflect the complexities and sensitivities of the proposed mining sites.
The result? Mines, encroaching dangerously close to crucial water sources.
BREATHE
Like Newcastle’s Chelmsford dam, which provides drinking water to thousands of people.

COMMENTARY
SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312
MVI_2977
19:01:59:33
“An opencast mine right next to a water source for Agriculture and more mining coming up in the background”

SUPER@ANGUS BURNG: WWF

MVI_2892

the war in Ukraine pushed a spike in the coal price and it ended up in many many, particularly smaller mining houses, trying to access the coal market”

VO

SUPER@ANGUS BURNG: WWF
“Small mines come in, they don’t have the financial fire power to rehabilitate the damage that they cause. At the end of the day what is left is a massive legacy for the tax payer, for municipalities and a very very short term gain for the shareholder of these mining companies”

PART 2

VO
But, as if water quality being threatened by people with little to no mining experience wasn’t bad enough, the area’s farmers are feeling the pressure, too. It’s putting food security at risk as mines push ever closer to agricultural land.

SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER
SOURCE: MVI_2806
16:17:18:46
“There has to be mining. But it is the way in which it disturbs our water, it infringes in our rights as farmers”

VO
Reginald Mabuza owns a commercial farm about 100 kilometres outside Newcastle. He is battling to prevent an adjacent mine from encroaching onto his land.

SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER
SOURCE: MVI_2836
16:45:39:25
“These guys, in front of their eyes, we are nothing, we are just subhuman because they’ve got the mining rights and us as the landowners the surface rights holders, we don’t have a say”

VO
Landowners only have surface rights, meaning the State owns everything beneath the surface – including any minerals.

SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER
SOURCE: MVI_2836
16:53:47:30
“So, what supersedes what? Surface rights or the mining rights? Once they got the mining rights, they just become gods”.

VO
It’s left Reginald powerless to protect what he spent a lifetime building.

SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER
SOURCE: MVI_2793
16:02:21:15
“This is the farm, Donkerhoek. It is in the Wakkerstroom area”

SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER
SOURCE: MVI_2793
16:08:33:44
“This is when I’m laying down there, six feet down, I will be proud of myself knowing, I bought a farm, my own farm. As you know the history of farms, blacks didn’t usually own farms in the past”.

VO
A legacy now hanging in the balance as the mine next door bulldozes through the boundaries.

SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER
SOURCE: MVI_2836
16:38:02:25
“They cut my fence, built their own gates, these poles are not my poles. They came in, they excavated this area. And this thing happened without my consent, there was no communication between me and the mine”

VO
The mine insisted Reginald’s fence was in the wrong place.

SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER
SOURCE: MVI_2836
16:40:43:26
“They came with papers, maps, they said it’s not your land, it’s our land. You guys have encroached to our land with 300 meters”.

SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER
SOURCE: MVI_2836
16:41:44:15
“Then from there, they said no, I have to get land surveyors, at my own cost to come and verify the perimeters.

SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER
SOURCE: MVI_2836
16:44:11:38
“This parameter had been like this, from 1968 October, 21. That is when the land surveyor general signed”.

VO
It seems a disregard for landowners by mining applicants is the norm here.
Burns says the problems begin during the prospecting phase.

SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312
MVI_2892

There absolutely are rights, and that is why there is consultation, that is why there is a process.
SUPER@ANGUS BURNG: WWF
SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312

we’re not seeing a fair and equitable, open and transparent process and we’re actually seeing that the process is not being done in the interest of the public or the environment”


PART 3

VO
The environmental impact of the mines must be assessed and documented. But that’s where the lines blur. The consultants who conduct the assessment are paid by the mining companies.

SUPER@ANGUS BURNG: WWF
SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312
MVI_2892
17:41:29:36
they say that they are objective, but when I object because of these reasons, they turn around and say well, we’re going to push this through anyway”

VO
The government relies on the consultants' reports in deciding whether to grant mining rights.
PAUSE
While in Newcastle, we were told a mining company called Slydeb intends mining on the border of one of its suburbs – and the locals aren’t happy!
Slydeb hired Singo Consulting who had to arrange a public meeting.

MVI_2892

Like the community, we also had questions about the people behind Slydeb.
PAUSE
And it didn't take us long to find its sole director: Yandisa Debedu… She and her husband had previously used Singo consulting in eight other attempts to get mining rights.
Slydeb is a typical example of small companies appearing across the coal belt…mostly without any previous mining experience… or knowledge of sustainability and rehabilitation.

Farmers near the water rich Drakensberg are threatened by opportunist coal miners trying to strip their land. But who gives these companies the rights to mine?

Is Newcastle on the brink of becoming another coal mining town?

nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 31 March 2024 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Press Release: Digging for Coal In KwaZulu-Natal, commercial farmers are on edge. While they own the land they farm on, government owns the minerals that lie underneath, and it’s giving scores of upstart coal companies prospecting licences and rights to mine. Tensions between farmers and mining groups in Newcastle are at an all-time high as the coal prospectors move in by the dozen to mine what’s left of the area’s coal reserve. For farmers, what’s equally concerning is the risk to vital water sources like the town’s main dam, which provides drinking water to hundreds of thousands of people. Who are these opportunistic mining companies and why are they being allowed to mine in sensitive and protected areas? Producer: Anina Peens | Presenter: Erin Bates | Research: Laura Byrne Script: NEWCASTLE PART 1 SOURCE: MVII_2883 and MVI_2888 UPSOUND; SOME KIND OF MEDITATIONAL MUSIC AND THE SHOT OF THE DRAKENSBERG TO CREATE A FEELING OF MAGNITUDE AND BEAUTY AND THEN THE FRESH WATER VO This is some of the purest water on earth. BREATHER The spring of one of our major river systems. SUPER@ANGUS BURNG: WWF SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_2892 17:29:34:30 “Right now, we are at the headwaters of the headwaters of the Tugela system… VISUAL: ANGUS AND ERIN COMES WALKING DOWN THE MOUNTAIN… SUPER@ANGUS BURNG: WWF SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_2892 17:29:34:30 “…right at the top where everything starts” VO We’re with Angus Burns - an environmentalist with the World Wildlife Fund - in the Northern Drakensberg, where he works to get sites like these declared protected. SUPER@ANGUS BURNG: WWF SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_2892 17:52:25:46 10 percent of the surface area of south Africa provides 50% of our water needs. That is our lifeblood VO Securing the country’s drinking water is at the heart of Burns’ mission. (PAUSE) A daunting task around Newcastle in KZN. VISUAL: COAL MINE VO Coal… The backbone of the economy… but the dirtiest of any mining processes. BREATHE Many inexperienced yet ambitious mining companies want to cash in. Creating a sight best appreciated from the air. BREATHER? OR MOMENT SUPER@ANGUS BURNG: WWF SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_2892 17:50:42:21 “I’ve seen maps of Mpumalanga province and northern KZN. It’s just a puzzle of little dots and spots showing cadasters of farms that are under prospecting and mining rights and literally zero strategic thinking given to the location of these sites in relation to water source areas” VO In recent years, small operators have been popping up across a vast area stretching from Newcastle, across the border into Mpumalanga. Many of the permit holders are small businesses without much mining experience. LINK/PROMO SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_2968 18:56:08:40 “We’re at the foothills of the Drakensberg and coal prospectors are carving into the earth down below. Question is, once they leave, is this just going to be a graveyard of coal mines?” VO Environmental impact assessments carried out before mining can start often don’t fully reflect the complexities and sensitivities of the proposed mining sites. The result? Mines, encroaching dangerously close to crucial water sources. BREATHE Like Newcastle’s Chelmsford dam, which provides drinking water to thousands of people. COMMENTARY SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_2977 19:01:59:33 “An opencast mine right next to a water source for Agriculture and more mining coming up in the background” SUPER@ANGUS BURNG: WWF SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_2892 17:31:31:35 the war in Ukraine pushed a spike in the coal price and it ended up in many many, particularly smaller mining houses, trying to access the coal market” VO Angus says there are currently more than 2500 new mining permit applications pending nationally. SUPER@ANGUS BURNG: WWF “Small mines come in, they don’t have the financial fire power to rehabilitate the damage that they cause. At the end of the day what is left is a massive legacy for the tax payer, for municipalities and a very very short term gain for the shareholder of these mining companies” PART 2 VO But, as if water quality being threatened by people with little to no mining experience wasn’t bad enough, the area’s farmers are feeling the pressure, too. It’s putting food security at risk as mines push ever closer to agricultural land. SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER SOURCE: MVI_2806 16:17:18:46 “There has to be mining. But it is the way in which it disturbs our water, it infringes in our rights as farmers” VO Reginald Mabuza owns a commercial farm about 100 kilometres outside Newcastle. He is battling to prevent an adjacent mine from encroaching onto his land. SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER SOURCE: MVI_2836 16:45:39:25 “These guys, in front of their eyes, we are nothing, we are just subhuman because they’ve got the mining rights and us as the landowners the surface rights holders, we don’t have a say” VO Landowners only have surface rights, meaning the State owns everything beneath the surface – including any minerals. SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER SOURCE: MVI_2836 16:53:47:30 “So, what supersedes what? Surface rights or the mining rights? Once they got the mining rights, they just become gods”. VO It’s left Reginald powerless to protect what he spent a lifetime building. SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER SOURCE: MVI_2793 16:02:21:15 “This is the farm, Donkerhoek. It is in the Wakkerstroom area” SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER SOURCE: MVI_2793 16:08:33:44 “This is when I’m laying down there, six feet down, I will be proud of myself knowing, I bought a farm, my own farm. As you know the history of farms, blacks didn’t usually own farms in the past”. VO A legacy now hanging in the balance as the mine next door bulldozes through the boundaries. SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER SOURCE: MVI_2836 16:38:02:25 “They cut my fence, built their own gates, these poles are not my poles. They came in, they excavated this area. And this thing happened without my consent, there was no communication between me and the mine” VO The mine insisted Reginald’s fence was in the wrong place. SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER SOURCE: MVI_2836 16:40:43:26 “They came with papers, maps, they said it’s not your land, it’s our land. You guys have encroached to our land with 300 meters”. SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER SOURCE: MVI_2836 16:41:44:15 “Then from there, they said no, I have to get land surveyors, at my own cost to come and verify the perimeters. SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER SOURCE: MVI_2836 16:44:11:38 “This parameter had been like this, from 1968 October, 21. That is when the land surveyor general signed”. VO It seems a disregard for landowners by mining applicants is the norm here. Burns says the problems begin during the prospecting phase. SUPER@ANGUS BURNG: WWF SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_2892 17:56:31:43 There absolutely are rights, and that is why there is consultation, that is why there is a process. SUPER@ANGUS BURNG: WWF SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_2892 17:41:29:36 we’re not seeing a fair and equitable, open and transparent process and we’re actually seeing that the process is not being done in the interest of the public or the environment” PART 3 VO The environmental impact of the mines must be assessed and documented. But that’s where the lines blur. The consultants who conduct the assessment are paid by the mining companies. SUPER@ANGUS BURNG: WWF SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_2892 17:41:29:36 they say that they are objective, but when I object because of these reasons, they turn around and say well, we’re going to push this through anyway” VO The government relies on the consultants' reports in deciding whether to grant mining rights. PAUSE While in Newcastle, we were told a mining company called Slydeb intends mining on the border of one of its suburbs – and the locals aren’t happy! Slydeb hired Singo Consulting who had to arrange a public meeting. STRAP: AMATEUR FOOTAGE SOURCE: MEETING 1 00:00:35:28 “So based on what you guys have been saying that you don’t want the mine or prospecting happening in your place…” VO These environmental assessment practitioners from Singo were met by strong opposition when they attempted to hijack a ward council meeting. SOURCE: MEETING 4 00:17 “Bunch of frauds trying to open a flippen coal mine on our front stoep” 04:58 HOEKOM KOM HULLE NA ONS PLEK TOE DAN DOEN HULLE ILLEGAL GOED? VO Who exactly is Slydeb they wanted to know, a question Singo ignored. SUPER@ANGUS BURNG: WWF SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_2892 17:43:45:20 “When you’re moving into a sensitive area, where people’s homes are at risk, there are sensitive environments, water source areas, you have a right to question the credibility of the company that is running this process”. VO Like the community, we also had questions about the people behind Slydeb. PAUSE And it didn't take us long to find its sole director: Yandisa Debedu… She and her husband had previously used Singo consulting in eight other attempts to get mining rights. Slydeb is a typical example of small companies appearing across the coal belt…mostly without any previous mining experience… or knowledge of sustainability and rehabilitation. SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_3034 19:44:11:16 ERIN: They’re really not very complicated questions, we can get through them on the phone” YANDI: I am driving my dear and I always prefer to have written communication…I will send you an email. ERIN: You will send us an email? So don’t you then need my email address? YANDI: Like I said, I am driving. we just want to understand what is your background in mining. 19:45:38:15 “All consultations were done, Erin, can you please wait for my email” VO All consultations were done? SUPER@EHRARD VAN ROOYEN: FARMER SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_3035 19:55:58:00 “Niemand daar was gekonsulteer nie, en almal was ongelukkig daaroor en al die boere wat geaffekteer sou gewees het, was nie eers by die vergadering nie” SUB: “Nobody was consulted and everybody was unhappy. Most affected farmers were not even at that meeting” VO Farmer Ehrard van Rooyen, much like Mabuza, feels utterly ignored. SUPER@EHRARD VAN ROOYEN: FARMER SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_3035 19:58:12:38 “Die oomblik as hulle gaan begin myn, al is dit om die plaas, dan beteken die plaas niks, hierdie is ‘n familieplaas en dit is vir my kinders en dit is vir hulle nageslag” SUB: The moment that they start mining, even if it is around my farm, then this farm is worthless. This is a family farm and it belongs to my children and their successors. VO Mining here will decimate agricultural land. SUPER@ANGUS BURNG: WWF SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_2892 17:30:59:13 “We are in a grasslands biome. Grasslands have evolved over thousands of years to be what they are…once that is damaged, you can grow some grass, but you can never restore it to what it was and you lose that biodiversity essentially for the next 3/400 years” VO Ehrard discovered these markers on his land, indicating that it was being considered for mining - it’s in in the area where Singo and Slydeb are operating. SUPER@EHRARD VAN ROOYEN: FARMER SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_3035 20:01:19:19 “Die mense het definitief sonder toestemming hier gekom, so hulle het definietief oortree. as hulle hier ingekom het het hulle deur die drade gekom of om die hek, of oor die hek” SUB: These people came here without permission, so they have trespassed. If they came in here they would have had to come through the fence or over the gate” VO Ehrard went to the ward meeting to get answers. Why was his land marked without his knowledge? Singo promised to arrange a proper consultation meeting with affected landowners. UPSOUND SOURCE: MEETING 3 00:00:13:00 “We hereby acknowledge that we do not consider this as a public participation meeting” VO But Singo’s head office told our producer the community didn’t give them an opportunity during the ward council meeting, so they saw no point in arranging a formal consultation. VOICE OF RUDZANI RADEBE SOURCE: AUDIO FILE ONLY 00:12:52:18 “Now that it didn’t work out, shouldn’t you call for a participation of the community?” “Can you give me a reason why we have to call again? VOICE OF RUDZANI RADEBE SOURCE: AUDIO FILE ONLY 00:01:37:17 “We spoke individually with landowners. So we met few landowners whom they were willing to engage then thereafter, there was, I don’t know, there is like a runner or a spokesperson for the whole community” 00:03:23:15 “The person who was giving out all the information came prepared with his own presentation. Our team had to stand there for an hour listening to that guy misleading everyone. ANINA: Do you know who this guy is? “Who is he?” ANINA: His name is Angus Burns, he works for the world wildlife fund. 00:13:17:14 “He should be wise enough not to mislead people by giving them false information” VO Singo say they’ll push for a permit despite concerns about how the mine will affect water security. 00:09:07:00 “Honestly speaking, I am not interested in this call anymore” 00:05:52:02 “At the end of the day, it’s the minerals of the department or for the government” VO Still none the wiser, we contacted company CEO, Dr Kenneth Singo. A man facing a criminal charge of fraud for allegedly copying and pasting an environmental management report from a different environmental consultant while pushing for mining rights on the border of the Kruger National Park. After sending him a list of questions, he declined to participate in what he called “our narrative”. SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_3016 19:29:19:11 “Good day Doctor Singo, this is Erin Bates from Carte Blanche…. 19:30:04:40 KENNETH “You can write whatever you want because I can see already on your email you have information that are not even true” ERIN: That is why we want to speak to you, to understand what your perspective is on these issues KENNETH “But you have already written the things that is why I am saying, proceed. ERIN: But Doctor Singo these are very serious allegations against you… KENNETH: So now I don’t want to comment, Ill wait for advise from our attorneys. 19:30:55:45 ERIN: you cannot comment at this stage? But doctor Singo, you’re busy practising while you’re facing criminal allegations? PHONE TONE VO Despite numerous attempts, we never heard from either Yandisa or Dr Singo again. BREATHE And while the whole world is moving towards greener energy, it seems South Africa is still risking valuable farmland and scarce water resources to benefit a select few. SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER SOURCE: MVI_2757 15:39:13:13 “Our government is pushing for people of my color to come into farming space” 15:39:52:42 But if this is happening then we lose this natural resource, SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER SOURCE: MVI_2806 16:17:18:46 a mine has got a lifespan of 10 years, 15 years SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER SOURCE: MVI_2806 16:18:17:21 After 20 years, the mine will be gone,what is gonna happen to the generation that comes?” TUESDAY PRESENTER PROMO SOURCE: DCIM?199_0311 MVI_2812 “Imagine going from this lush vibrant rain forest… MVI_2866/2868 “To this, drab, industrious mound of coal” VO Farmers near the water rich Drakensberg are threatened by opportunist coal miners trying to strip their land. But who gives these companies the rights to mine? TIMELINE PROMOS PROMO 1 Water and food security hang in the balance in Newcaslte district as young mining companies move in to delve for coal reserves. SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER SOURCE: MVI_2826 16:33:39:46 “This is just another picture of what is happening here” SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER SOURCE: MVI_2826 16:32:22:47 “This stream was live the water was running capacity wise it was big, but after the mines started this side, the water levels just dropped” VO Commercial farmers concerned as several mining companies dig for coal. PROMO 2 Are farmers and mining companies in a turf war in the New castle district? SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER SOURCE: MVI_2836 16:40:43:26 “They came with papers, maps, they said to my brother, no, you guys, where we have excavated, in fact, it’s not your land, it’s our land…” VO Tensions rise as new mining companies speculate on agricultural land. PROMO 3 Farmers and mining companies near Newcastle in a tug of war over new prospecting applications. SUPER@REGINALD MABUZA, FARMER SOURCE: MVI_2836 16:53:47:30 “SO, WHAT SUPERSEDES WHAT? SURFACE RIGHTS OR THE MINING RIGHTS? ONCE THEY GOT THE MINING RIGHTS, THEY JUST BECOME GODS”. VO Farmers say coal companies are threatening their survival and national food and water security. PROMO 4 Tension between farmers and young mining companies on the rise in Newcastle as the rush for coal intensifies. SUPER@EHRARD VAN ROOYEN: FARMER SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_3035 19:54:32:24 “Ek het met ‘n paar boere gepraat, en sover my kennis strek stel niemand belang dat daar gemyn moet word nie” SUB: “I spoke to a few farmers and as far as I know, no one wants mining here” VO Farmers say environmental companies, tasked to assess the land, are not playing by the rules. UPSOUND SOURCE: MEETING 4 14:17 LEAVE AND DON’T COME BACK, WE DON’T WANT YOU HERE. PROMO 5 There are about 6000 defunct and ownerless mines in South Africa. SUPER@ANGUS BURNG: WWF SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_2892 17:54:23:19 “…and we’ve got two and a half thousand pending mines on the horizon?” VO Tensions in Newcastle at boiling point as inexperienced companies’ prospect amidst a global movement away from fossil fuel SUPER@ANGUS BURNG: WWF SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_2892 17:31:52:18 “There is a global movement away from coal but there is an opportunity for small mining houses and individuals who want to make a lot of money really quickly, to try and access that few remaining coal reserves that exist, before essentially become obsolete”. PROMO 6 VO It’s a get-rich-quick rush to get to the remaining coal reserves. SUPER@ANGUS BURNG: WWF SOURCE: DCIM\200_0312 MVI_2892 17:32:28:35 “There is a proliferation of small mining concerns, mining houses, shelf companies that have been established to access the market. In many instances, they don’t have experience, they might have worked as mine manager, and they see the opportunity to make money. If you compare them to the big players, you will find that many of these big companies don’t operate in this space. So, the really big companies have divested off their coal interests because they know, coal is on the out. And what we have now are these small operators with very little experience with very little financial muscle, coming into the area, and in particular into sensitive areas, wanting to mine there and leaving massive legacy issues for us to deal with”. VO Is Newcastle on the brink of becoming another coal mining town?
